content: 1. Rodriguez-Perez MA and colleagues conducted a study comparing the sensitivity of antibody detection tests for Onchocerca volvulus. They evaluated a cocktail of recombinant antigens used in an indirect enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) against a rapid-format antibody card test. This study was published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2011. 2. Pischke S and colleagues developed an internal control for detecting Onchocerca volvulus DNA using PCR-ELISA. They also introduced a rapid detection method for specific PCR products using DNA detection test strips. This work was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2002. 3. Vincent JA and colleagues compared newer diagnostic tests for onchocerciasis. Their findings were published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 2000. 4. Toe L and colleagues utilized O-150 polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of skin snips to detect Onchocerca volvulus infection. This study was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1998. 5. Fischer P and colleagues assessed the sensitivity of a PCR-based assay for detecting Onchocerca volvulus DNA in skin biopsies. Their findings were published in Parasitology Research in 1996. 6. Zimmerman PA and colleagues improved the detection of Onchocerca volvulus infection using a PCR-based diagnostic approach. Their study was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 1994. 7. Boateng BA and colleagues compared three diagnostic methods for detecting Onchocerca volvulus infection in low-prevalence areas. Their findings were published in Parasitology in 2002. 8. Rodriguez-Perez MA and colleagues developed a high-throughput automated DNA isolation method for detecting Onchocerca volvulus in Latin American black flies using pool screening PCR. This study was published in Parasitology Research in 2013. 9. Gopal H and colleagues introduced an oligonucleotide-based magnetic bead capture method for isolating Onchocerca volvulus DNA for PCR pool screening of vector black flies. This work was published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2012. 10. Rodriguez-Perez MA and colleagues compared a PCR assay with fly dissection for detecting Onchocerca volvulus infection in Simulium ochraceum sensu lato in a hypoendemic Mexican community. This study was published in Parasitology in 1999. 11. Yameogo L and colleagues conducted a field trial using pool screen PCR to estimate the prevalence of Onchocerca volvulus infection in Simulium damnosum sensu lato in an area with successful vector control. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1999. 12. Rodriguez-Perez MA and colleagues compared serological and parasitological assessments of Onchocerca volvulus transmission after seven years of mass ivermectin treatment in Mexico. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 1999. 13. Katabarwa MN and colleagues evaluated the implementation of community-directed treatment with ivermectin for onchocerciasis control in Uganda between 1997 and 2000. Their findings were published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 2002. 14. Brieger WR and colleagues investigated gender and ethnic differences in onchocercal skin disease in Oyo State, Nigeria. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 1997. 15. Mutalemwa P and colleagues explored the use of a community-directed approach beyond ivermectin in Tanzania as a mechanism for delivering complex health interventions. Their findings were published in the Tanzania Journal of Health Research in 2009. 16. Makauula P and colleagues conducted a qualitative assessment of primary health care in rural Malawi, focusing on the relevance of the community-directed interventions approach. This study was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2012. 17. Boatin B reviewed the Onchocerciasis Control Programme (OCP) in West Africa, highlighting its achievements and challenges. This review was published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 2008. 18. Keating J and colleagues conducted a systematic review of the costs associated with the prevention, treatment, and control of lymphatic filariasis and onchocerciasis across diverse settings. Their findings were published in Acta Tropica in 2014. 19. WHO/OCP developed training modules for national entomologists and technicians to manage and supervise entomological activities in onchocerciasis control. These modules were published in 2002. 20. Guidelines for certifying the elimination of onchocerciasis in Uganda were developed and accessed in November 2015. 21. A manual for monitoring and epidemiological assessment of mass drug administration in the Global Programme to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis was published to guide national elimination programs. 22. Plaisier AP and colleagues developed ONCHOSIM, a model and computer simulation program for studying the transmission and control of onchocerciasis. This work was published in Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine in 1990. 23. Davies JB described a computer model of forest onchocerciasis transmission and its application to field scenarios involving vector control and chemotherapy. This study was published in Annals of Tropical Medicine and Parasitology in 1993. 24. Mills RA applied a quantitative approach to study the epidemiology of onchocerciasis in West Africa. This work was published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1969. 25. Wada Y proposed a theoretical approach to studying the epidemiology of onchocerciasis in Guatemala. This study was published in the Japanese Journal of Medical Science and Biology in 1982. 26. Dietz K analyzed the population dynamics of onchocerciasis in a chapter of the book The Population Dynamics of Infectious Diseases: Theory and Applications, edited by RM Anderson and published by Chapman & Hall in 1982. 27. Basáñez MG and Ricardez-Esquinca J reviewed models for the population biology and control of human onchocerciasis. This review was published in Trends in Parasitology in 2001. 28. Winnen M and colleagues evaluated the potential of ivermectin mass treatments to eliminate onchocerciasis in Africa. Their findings were published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2002. 29. Duerr HP and colleagues analyzed threshold shifts, breakpoints, and rules for the elimination of onchocerciasis in Africa. This study was published in the International Journal of Parasitology in 2011. 30. Collins RC studied the transmission potential of onchocerciasis in four species of Guatemalan Simuliidae. This work was published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 1979. 31. A roadmap for accelerating efforts to overcome the global impact of neglected tropical diseases was published and accessed in December 2015.
